title: One climb and out: 900m D+, fuelling test carrying it
terrain: alpine, ONE sustained climb ~900m D+, descent hard-capped 600m, lift-assisted down if available

steps.target: Z2-Z3 single sustained climb ~900m D+, 84-89% LTHR
Z1-Z2 descent, capped 600m, poles, cadence 175+, 55-80% LTHR

coachNotes: OPTIMAL LOAD RULE, THE GOVERNING GATE FROM 24 AUG: a session passes only if it produces no symptoms during it, none immediately after, and none the next day. Any one of the three is a fail, and the next session drops back to the last level that passed. The ceiling during a run is 2/10 with no spike afterwards; mild is allowed, new or worsening is not. This replaces every softer wording elsewhere in this plan. GAIT, MEASURED FROM THE 22 AUG CADENCE STREAM ON 24 AUG. Your descent cadence is already good and is NOT the problem: 177 spm on grades steeper than -20%, 179 spm across the second half of the sustained descents, 176 on the final descent to the door. Do not change it, and do not let anyone tell you to. THE EXPOSURE IS FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL: 152 spm on flat ground and 156 spm at -3 to -10%. That is precisely the gradient band where the knee spends longest inside the 20-30 degree compression zone under load, it is the running you do most of, and the final 1250m into Bansko is full of it. TARGET 165-170 spm ON FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL, a 5-10% lift, which is the range the gait-retraining literature uses. Metronome or a 165 bpm playlist. Shorter steps at the same effort; do not convert it into more pace. STEP WIDTH: run slightly wider than feels natural, not on a tightrope. Narrow step width raises ITB strain and strain rate directly and it is one of the few things you can change inside 19 days. DOWNGRADED 24 AUG, THE ARMED CONTINGENCY HAS FIRED. 195 -> 130, D+ 1600 -> 900, D- cap 1200 -> 600, two climbs -> one. The trigger written on 23 August was 'any band signal Monday or Tuesday'. Monday evening produced intermittent pin sensations at the right lateral knee while walking, which is provocation at a lower load threshold than the running criterion I wrote, and therefore a stronger signal rather than a weaker one. This session is not restored without 10 consecutive symptom-free days including running. THE FUELLING OBJECTIVE IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE DAY: 80 g/h held from minute 30 to the finish, measured. If holding the intake means cutting the route further, cut the route. A day that returns 900m and a verified 80 g/h is a success; a day that returns 900m and 30 g/h is a wasted last chance. TAKE THE LIFT DOWN IF THERE IS ONE. The 600m cap is the route, not your discipline: fixed line, fixed endpoint, load the GPX, no summit out-and-backs. FUELLING TARGET RAISED 60 -> 80 g/h ON 24 AUG, SUPERSEDING EVERY 60 g/h FIGURE BELOW. The product question left open on 23 August is answered: Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro is 40g per gel at 2:1 glucose-fructose, so the single-transporter ceiling that justified the 60 target does not bind. At 80 g/h you sit at roughly 53g glucose and 27g fructose an hour, inside both limits. THE RACE SYSTEM TO REHEARSE TODAY: one 65g sachet of Enervit Isocarb C2:1 Pro per 500ml bottle per hour is 60g of carbohydrate and 600mg of sodium, isotonic, and it hits the sodium target exactly. Add one 40g Carbo Gel every second hour and the total is 80 g/h. Over 4h30 that is 4 bottles and 2 gels instead of 9 gels; the same arithmetic over 8 hours on race day is 8 sachets and 4 gels instead of 16 gels and 1.1kg of packaging. If the Isocarb has not arrived, run today on 2 Carbo Gels an hour with 200ml of water each, and order it before 12 September. TODAY IS THE DURATION TEST. 29 August established whether 80 g/h goes down at all; today establishes whether it goes down for four and a half hours, which is the number that predicts hour six at Pirin. WRITE IT DOWN: grams per hour, product, and what the stomach did at hour three and hour four. The 60 g/h target below and the reasoning for it are superseded; the delivery discipline is not. Feed every 30 minutes, carbohydrate in the bottle, sodium 500-700 mg/h. PURPOSE CHANGED 23 AUG: THIS IS NOW A FUELLING TEST THAT HAPPENS TO HAVE 1600m OF CLIMBING IN IT. The 22 August rehearsal returned a clean stomach on 21-29 g/h against a 60-90 g/h prescription, roughly a third of race intake, so the gut was never actually tested and the number that matters is still unknown. Energy that day was 2856 kcal out against 424-600 kcal in, a deficit larger than total glycogen stores, which is the most likely explanation for RPE 9 on a session whose heart rate sat at 84% of LTHR. PRIMARY OBJECTIVE, ranked above the vertical: hold 60 g/h from minute 30 to the finish, measured, with the products you will race on. If holding 60 g/h means cutting the route short, cut the route. A day that returns 1600m of climbing and 25 g/h is a failed session; a day that returns 1100m and a verified 60 g/h is a successful one. TARGET IS 60 g/h AND NOT 90. Pirin at 38km and 3300m projects 8-9 hours and roughly 4400-5000 kcal; 60 g/h closes about half of that, which is what a finish looks like, and it is reachable from a 25 g/h baseline in three weeks whereas 90 is not. Ninety also needs glucose-fructose blends to clear the single-transporter ceiling around 60 g/h, so if the gels are glucose or maltodextrin only, 60 is the hard ceiling regardless of gut training. DELIVERY, because four feeds in five hours is the mechanism that failed, not the willingness: feed every 30 minutes, not every 60, and put carbohydrate in the bottle. 2.5 litres of plain water on 22 August was 2.5 litres of wasted carrier. One 500ml bottle at 80g of drink mix sipped over two hours is 40 g/h with nothing to chew, plus a gel each hour lands 65 g/h without any change in willpower. SODIUM: 500-700 mg per hour, which was missing entirely on 22 August. Five hours cool was fine; nine hours warm on plain water is how you arrive at the last climb dizzy. WEEK 7 IS THE GUT TRAINING WINDOW and it is flat, so there is nothing else for it to do. Take 60 g/h on every run over 60 minutes, easy ones included. Intestinal transporter capacity adapts over roughly two weeks of repeated exposure; three weeks from now is enough for a partial adaptation and not enough if it starts on 5 September. WRITE IT DOWN: grams per hour, product, and what the stomach did at hour three and hour four. Everything below this line still applies. CUT 235 -> 195, D+ 2000 -> 1600, D- cap 1500 -> 1200, on 21 August. This is the other half of the trade that made 22 August bigger. Load placed 21 days out is cheap and load placed 7 days out is expensive, and the version of this plan that put the biggest single day here was betting the taper on a session that had no week behind it to absorb. Start-line numbers barely move: CTL 44.0 against a 42 target, TSB +7.6 rather than +5.9, so the rebalance costs 0.4 fitness points and buys 1.7 points of freshness. THE PRECONDITION IS GONE, WHICH IS THE REAL POINT. The 2000m version required real eccentric work through week 7 in Milan and Belgium to be safe, and travel weeks eat that kind of promise. At 1600m D+ / 1200m D- this session sits below 22 August's 1400m of descent, so the eccentric ramp across the 14-day flat gap is negative rather than positive. Do the week 7 work anyway, it makes this day better, but the plan no longer breaks if you miss it. DESCENT CAP 1200m, STILL NOT NEGOTIABLE. Point-to-point finishing ~400m above the start, or take a lift down the last section. If the only option is a loop with matched D-, the day becomes 1300m D+ / 1300m D-: the descent cap outranks the climb target, every time. THE CAP IS THE ROUTE, NOT YOUR DISCIPLINE. Fixed line, fixed endpoint, load the GPX. No extensions, no summit out-and-backs. Finishing strong is the session working, not an invitation. WHAT THIS BUYS: 48% of race vertical at roughly race gradient, ~4h20 on your feet, the second fuelling rehearsal seven days out, and the knowledge that the legs come back from 22 August. It is not fitness. CTL is already past target and one session cannot move it. FUELLING: full race kit, nothing new, 60-90g carbs per hour from minute 40. Compare against what you wrote down on 22 August and fix whatever went wrong then. AMBER: HRV 7d/28d under 0.90 or any lateral knee signal on Thursday or Friday means one climb and out, ~900m D+, load 130. Garmin expect 320-380.
